name: Forgotten History
description: CorpChat's internal code mirror is exposed at /challenge/. Dig into the repository history — what the developers removed might still be recoverable.
hints: The .git/ directory is browseable. Try reconstructing the full commit history using the object store.

name: Stolen Identity
description: You're registered but limited. A platform search feature has a vulnerability that can expose data it shouldn't. Once you escalate your access, look for what other accounts are leaking.
hints: There are multiple search queries running on the backend. Not all of them are parameterised. Look at what the results section of the page renders when you get a hit.

name: Backdoor Access
description: After gaining a shell you find an internal admin binary locked away in /data/uploads/tools/. Move it somewhere accessible and reverse engineer it — the developer left something useful inside.
hints: The binary encodes its strings with a simple symmetric cipher. Find the key — it's hardcoded.

name: Legacy Secrets
description: The platform stores passwords using an old hashing scheme for backwards compatibility. Once you have database access, crack the hash for a specific account. The answer is the flag. Submit it as CTF{...}
hints: The legacy_password_hash column uses a two-step scheme. Think about what transformations are applied after hashing.

name: Go-Root-Yourself
description: You have a low-privilege shell as the service account. A cron job runs as root every minute in a directory you control. That's all you need.
hints: What happens when tar encounters a filename that starts with --? Check /etc/cron.d/ for the full command.
